labels.label: theo:CBG
labels.notes: Unmarked, partial (abstract Geometry, DEC-134). theo_CBG asserts ETT's sentence fully: some Mbar is IsCEMaximal (and universal), and every IsCEMaximal M is isomorphic to it by a unique morphism whose inverse is a morphism. The extra hypothesis, a Cauchy surface S of M0, is disclosed. theo_CBG_of_modelMeasures replaces it with the named hypothesis ModelMeasures (kb/0012), which is also disclosed. T2, connected and SC on M0 match def:singular_spacetime (connected manifold). IsCEMaximal is not vacuous: existence is asserted, and Dev.isCEMaximal_iff makes it equal to IsETTMaximal through Dev.IsMorphism.injective. The closure of theo_CBG uses rigid, germExt_* and slice_* (probed), which agrees with SCOPE. Finding l.2336-2340 checked: a directed colimit of T2 spaces need not be T2, and the paper itself concedes the proper-class issue in rem:CBG_manquant(ii).

labels.label: rem:CBG_analytique
labels.notes: Unmarked, partial. Geometry.rigid_univ restates the field A1 at V = top, with a T2 target and a connected source, as the remark's sentence ('defined on a connected manifold'); manifolds are Hausdorff. Claim 1 (analyticity) is cited and not formalized, which is disclosed. The finding about Hausdorffness needing A3/A4 is a statement about the formal route. It does not exhibit a geometry where rigidity alone fails to give T2, and should be read as that, not as a refutation of the remark.

labels.label: lem:corresponding_K
labels.notes: ett_corresponding_K: p in frontier(range b) ∩ J+(Σ1) and q in frontier(range c) ∩ J+(Σ2), and (p,q) in the literal C iff (K-(p) ∩ J+(Σ1) ⊆ j1(N) and BijOn f ...). The extra conjunct only makes explicit the domain of f, which the paper presupposes, and lem:passe_pgcd gives it anyway. The direction is equivalent to the paper's. Confirmed by a transitive-constant probe that the proof uses none of germExt_*, slice_* or rigid (A2 only), as REPORT and SCOPE claim. The only open item is the E0 instance.

labels.label: cor:ext_continue
labels.notes: ett_ext_continue: for every (p,q) in the literal C (graph pairs included), update f p q is ContinuousWithinAt on insert p (range b) at p. This is the paper's 'f extends continuously to p by f(p)=q', with no restriction on p. The arbitrary extension of f off j1(N) does not matter. The proof-gap finding at l.2148-2156 (p is not assumed to be in J+(Σ1) when lem:corresponding_K is applied, and the compact-diamond claim is unsupported) is correct.

labels.label: cor:model_corresponding
labels.notes: Uniqueness of the partner for p in ∂j1(N) is faithful. The type assertion is stated as an iff for all α ≥ 0 (ℝ_+, def:singular_spacetime) but only under p ∈ ∂j1(N). The paper's 'Moreover, if (p,q) ∈ C ...' literally also covers graph pairs (p ∈ j1(N), where q = f(p)). Reading 'Moreover' as inheriting the corollary's p ∈ ∂j1(N) is natural and the omitted case is trivial (isMor_sing), but the REPORT does not disclose this reading (minor finding).

labels.label: prop:Cauchy_non_max
labels.notes: Falsity claim verified. Gluing.C is literally 'images not separated in Quot (GlueRel b c)' (Pushout.lean:321). Graph pairs have equal images, so they lie in C (graph_subset_C), and rem:non_separe_cas itself lists the graph case among the non-separated pairs. J(Σ1,p) = J+(Σ1) ∩ J-(p) (def:diamonds l.345, lem:image_diamant). For p = j1(x), causal convexity of j1(N) ⊇ Σ1 gives the printed hypothesis (ett_cauchy_point_min_literal, which holds for every x). N = mcghdSubDev is maximal in exactly ETT's sense (CommonSubDev.IsMaximal: every morphism out is bijective, mcghdSubDev_isMaximal), so the conclusion 'N not maximal' fails. ett_cauchy_non_max_literal_false holds over any geometry for non-empty connected M0. The _flat instance inhabits it (flat Minkowski, N against itself, a legitimate pair of Cauchy extensions), so it is not vacuous. The witness point is b(emb(arbitrary)) and is not shown to lie in J+(Σ1). That does not matter, because the inclusion holds for every x, Σ1 included. Intended form ett_cauchy_non_max (Cdist, diamond hypothesis dropped) is stronger than the printed one in that reading, as disclosed. The row is correctly partial and unmarked.

labels.label: prop:C_connexe
labels.notes: C1 open in ∂j1(N) is stated as C1 = W ∩ ∂j1(N) with W open. 'C closed in ∂×∂' is stated as C ∩ (∂×∂) closed in M1×M2, which implies the subspace statement. Faithful. The finding on the l.2303 gap is correct: C closed does not give C1 ∩ c_n closed in c_n without a compactness bound on the partners (a projection of a closed set).

labels.label: prop:Cauchy_point_min
labels.notes: Literal form proved (ett_cauchy_point_min_literal, with graph pairs as witnesses). This is correctly reported as true but uninformative. Intended Cdist forms proved. REPORT's hypothesis note says the proof 'uses A2 and A3', but the probe shows that the closure of ett_cauchy_point_min contains no germExt_*, slice_* or rigid (minor finding: over-stated dependency).

labels.label: prop:ppcm_Cauchy
labels.notes: CommonOverDev uses injective morphisms of developments into a Dev. These carry ι1(Σ) onto ι_P(Σ), so they are ETT's Cauchy embeddings, and P is GH as the definition of Cauchy embedding requires. IsMorphism, Equivalent and IsMinimal match l.1983-1985. ett_ppcm_Cauchy states that ppcmOver is minimal and that every minimal common over-extension is equivalent to it ('up to equivalence the unique minimal'). ConnectedSpace M0 gives Nonempty. The reading 'pgcd = MCGHD' is disclosed as a question.

labels.label: rem:CBG_manquant
labels.notes: Informal remark, partial. Dev.card_le_continuum proves ≤ 𝔠 where the paper says '= 𝔠'. This is disclosed as weakened, with equality not needed. ett_maximal_secondCountable is immediate from Dev.sc, as SCOPE discloses. The content is maxSpace_secondCountable through the field secondCountable_of_cauchy.
